answer.evidence: In radon/visitors.py, ComplexityVisitor.__init__ (line 157) takes no_assert=False and stores it as self.no_assert (line 165). visit_Assert (around lines 257-260) does `self.complexity += not self.no_assert`. The bool is added as 1 when assertion counting is enabled and as 0 when no_assert=True. The same flag is passed to nested ComplexityVisitor instances (line 279) and to methods (line 313). D gets the most time because it holds the logic. B (radon/complexity.py) gets the next largest share as the likely entry point that forwards no_assert, and C (radon/metrics.py) gets a smaller share as a consumer. A (radon/raw.py) has no assert-related code, so it gets the least time. I did not read the handoff_refs files, since the task says they are context only. I also did not open B or C, so their allocations are inferred from grep results and the file names.
